1.name: High Functioning / Well-Supported Seniors
1.interpretation: Strong WHO Healthy Ageing alignment across all domains. Senior is physically and psychologically resilient, financially stable, and socially engaged. Requires preventive monitoring only.

2.name: Stable Ageing / Moderate Support Needs
2.interpretation: Moderate alignment across Intrinsic Capacity, Environment, and Functional Ability. Some domains stable, others beginning to decline. May benefit from social activation programs and periodic health monitoring.

3.name: Environmentally and Financially Vulnerable Seniors
3.interpretation: Intrinsic Capacity and functional ability are relatively preserved, but environmental and financial stressors are significant. Priority: livelihood support, housing assistance, and access to social protection programs.

4.name: Low Functioning / Multi-Domain Priority Seniors
4.interpretation: Lowest WHO Healthy Ageing alignment across all domains. Multi-domain vulnerability in physical health, environment, and functional independence. Requires immediate multi-domain intervention and priority case management.
